reason: Two missing prerequisites prevent unattended autonomous execution of a real `hermes update` test even though all 9 lifecycle gates are green.

missing_prerequisites.name: Uncommitted local WIP in install tree
missing_prerequisites.evidence: `git -C ~/.hermes/hermes-agent status -sb` reports 5 untracked paths: commands/, skills/imported-claude-agents/, skills/tnf-full-auto-network-autopilot.skill, skills/tnf-full-auto-network-autopilot/, tinker-atropos/. These are NOT TNF work — they are external local changes that would be stashed/restored by `hermes update`, potentially disturbing another agent's WIP.
missing_prerequisites.block: The lifecycle lane is explicitly forbidden to absorb unrelated local WIP.

missing_prerequisites.name: `hermes update` triggers gateway restart
missing_prerequisites.evidence: `hermes update --help` describes 'restart every running Hermes service across all profiles'. The current shell session is itself spawned from a Hermes gateway context; restarting would terminate the agent session before any post-update reconcile receipt could be emitted.
missing_prerequisites.block: The mutation-authorization in this lane does not extend to terminating the executing shell session or interrupting other in-flight agent work.

alternative_proof: STAGE 2 rollback-proof tests already exercised the BASELINE -> SNAPSHOT -> MUTATE/OVERWRITE -> REDISCOVER -> DETECT DRIFT -> REPAIR/ROLLBACK -> VERIFY HASHES -> RECEIPT pipeline against the real LifecycleGuardian implementation on synthetic managed surfaces. Real vendor-mutation semantics are covered by the hermes-agent install tree containing the canonical AGENTS.md development contract plus the vendor's documented `git pull && reinstall` flow that has been observed in past updates.
